papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

The studies highlight the effectiveness of combining traditional text-mining techniques with deep learning approaches to address challenges in accuracy, interpretability, and contextual understanding in the processing of biomedical and document data.

It suggests further exploration into hybrid approaches that combine the strengths of GNNs, LLMs, and attention mechanisms to enhance knowledge extraction and classification accuracy.

summary: The literature on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge discovery emphasizes advancements in hybrid models that integrate GNNs with traditional text-mining techniques to enhance knowledge extraction and document classification in scientific literature. Key limitations include the computational expense of deep learning models and challenges in interpretability, particularly with transformer-based models. Notably, there is a research gap in developing more interpretable and efficient GNN models that can leverage document structure and contextual information, suggesting a need for empirical applications in diverse scientific domains. Additionally, the integration of machine learning in materials science, particularly in glass design, highlights the potential for GNNs to improve predictive modeling, which could be adapted for broader literature analysis.
literature_tension_graph: Current literature highlights a tension between the computational efficiency and interpretability of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in knowledge extraction tasks. While some studies (e.g., P2) demonstrate the effectiveness of hybrid models combining GNNs and structured ontology for biomedical literature, they also acknowledge issues with LLM hallucination and result interpretability. Conversely, other works (e.g., P3) emphasize improvements in document classification through deep learning without integrating GNNs, suggesting a gap in leveraging GNNs for enhanced contextual understanding. This presents an unresolved condition where existing models fail to reconcile the need for both efficiency and interpretability in diverse scientific domains. The research direction that emerges is the development of a novel GNN framework that effectively integrates attention mechanisms and structured ontology models to improve knowledge extraction while addressing these limitations.
scholarly_positioning: Current approaches to knowledge extraction in scientific literature primarily rely on traditional text-mining techniques and hybrid models that often overlook the structural and contextual nuances of documents. While advancements in GNNs have shown promise in specific domains, such as biomedical literature, there remains a significant gap in their application across diverse scientific fields, particularly in achieving interpretability and efficiency. Existing models frequently struggle with computational demands and the interpretability of results, leading to unresolved tensions in their practical deployment. This proposed research aims to develop a novel GNN framework that integrates structured ontology models and attention mechanisms, addressing these limitations and enhancing knowledge discovery by leveraging document structure and contextual information more effectively.
research_scope: This study will focus on the application of a novel Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework for knowledge extraction and document classification within biomedical literature. The target population will include a diverse range of scientific publications, specifically those related to protein interactions and disease mechanisms. The GNN model will integrate structured ontology models and attention mechanisms to enhance interpretability and efficiency in knowledge discovery. The evaluation period will encompass a comprehensive analysis of existing biomedical datasets over six months. The baseline for comparison will be traditional text-mining techniques and existing GNN models. Primary outcomes will include the accuracy of knowledge extraction measured by the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and F1 score, while secondary outcomes will assess interpretability scores and computational efficiency metrics. This research aims to bridge the gap in current methodologies by providing a more interpretable and efficient model for extracting knowledge from complex scientific literature.
concept_definition:
{
  "Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)": "A type of neural network designed to process data structured as graphs, capturing relationships and interactions between nodes (e.g., scientific concepts) for tasks like knowledge extraction.",
  "Knowledge Extraction": "The process of identifying and extracting relevant information from unstructured data sources, such as scientific literature, to create structured knowledge representations.",
  "Document Classification": "The task of categorizing documents into predefined classes based on their content, often using machine learning techniques to automate the process.",
  "Structured Ontology Models": "Formal representations of knowledge within a domain, consisting of concepts and their relationships, used to enhance the understanding of context in data processing.",
  "Attention Mechanisms": "Techniques in neural networks that allow the model to focus on specific parts of the input data, improving the relevance and interpretability of the output.",
  "Interpretability Scores": "Metrics that quantify how understandable a model's predictions are to humans, often assessed through user studies or specific interpretability methods.",
  "Computational Efficiency Metrics": "Measurements that evaluate the speed and resource consumption of a model during training and inference, important for scalability in large datasets.",
  "Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)": "A performance metric for binary classification that considers true and false positives and negatives, providing a balanced measure even with imbalanced datasets.",
  "F1 Score": "A harmonic mean of precision and recall, used to evaluate the accuracy of a model's classification performance, particularly in imbalanced classes.",
  "Interpretability Assessment Scores": "Quantitative evaluations of how well a model's decisions can be understood, often derived from user feedback or specific interpretability techniques.",
  "Overfitting": "A modeling error that occurs when a model learns the training data too well, capturing noise instead of the underlying pattern, leading to poor generalization on new data.",
  "Contextual Information Integration": "The process of incorporating relevant background knowledge or situational context into a model to improve its understanding and performance on specific tasks.",
  "Generalization": "The ability of a model to perform well on unseen data, indicating its robustness and applicability across different contexts or domains.",
  "User Trust": {
    "Trust Calibration": "The alignment between a user's confidence in a model's predictions and the actual accuracy of those predictions.",
    "Blind Trust": "A situation where users rely on a model's outputs without understanding its workings or limitations.",
    "Perceived Transparency": "The extent to which users feel they can understand how a model makes decisions, impacting their trust in the system.",
    "Appropriate Reliance": "The degree to which users depend on a model's outputs based on its demonstrated reliability and performance."
  },
  "Safety Outcomes": {
    "Unsafe Response Rate": "The frequency at which a model generates harmful or inappropriate outputs.",
    "Over-Refusal": "Instances where a model declines to provide an answer unnecessarily, potentially limiting user access to information.",
    "Jailbreak Success": "The ability of users to manipulate a model into providing restricted or unsafe outputs.",
    "Harmful Compliance": "When a model follows harmful instructions or prompts, leading to negative consequences.",
    "Refusal Precision/Recall": "Metrics assessing the accuracy of a model's refusals, indicating how well it identifies when to decline to answer."
  }
}
technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible, but it requires access to open-source GNN models for effective experimentation and potentially hidden state extraction for interpretability analysis. Labelled datasets from biomedical literature are essential for training and evaluation. Given the focus on user trust, a human-subject design will be necessary to assess appropriate reliance and trust calibration. Additionally, GPU resources will be required for model training and evaluation. To enhance feasibility, the study could consider using existing datasets with established annotation protocols to streamline the process.

question: How does the integration of attention mechanisms and structured ontology models within a Graph Neural Network framework improve the accuracy and interpretability of knowledge extraction and document classification in biomedical literature compared to traditional text-mining techniques?

It is theoretically meaningful, as it aims to reconcile existing tensions between computational demands and the need for contextual understanding in GNN applications. The problem is empirically testable through the proposed methodology, which includes measurable outcomes such as accuracy and interpretability scores. A PhD committee is likely to find this topic compelling due to its potential to advance knowledge discovery in diverse scientific domains. However, the strongest reason for potential rejection could be the perceived overlap with existing literature without clear empirical contributions. To enhance the research's depth, the problem could be reframed to focus specifically on the comparative analysis of GNN frameworks against traditional methods in varied scientific contexts, emphasizing the unique contributions to interpretability and contextual integration.

theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the integration of attention mechanisms and structured ontology models (independent variable) within a Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework to enhance knowledge extraction and document classification (dependent variable) in biomedical literature. The theoretical framework posits that the structured ontology models serve as a mediator by improving contextual understanding, while attention mechanisms moderate the relationship by focusing on relevant document features. This causal chain suggests that enhanced contextual understanding leads to improved accuracy and interpretability of knowledge extraction. System-level outcomes, such as computational efficiency and interpretability scores, are influenced by representation features of the GNN, while user-level outcomes, including trust and reliance, are mediated by perceived transparency. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of the structured ontology in diverse contexts and the impact of attention mechanisms on model interpretability.
hypothesis: Integrating attention mechanisms and structured ontology models within a Graph Neural Network framework (independent variable) will result in higher accuracy of knowledge extraction (primary dependent variable) compared to traditional text-mining techniques (baseline), with improved contextual understanding serving as a mediator that enhances this effect.

methodology: This study will employ a hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework for knowledge extraction and document classification in biomedical literature, utilizing structured ontology models and attention mechanisms. The target dataset will consist of annotated biomedical publications, focusing on protein interactions and disease mechanisms, ensuring diversity in content. The proposed GNN model will be compared against traditional text-mining techniques and existing GNN models as baselines. Key operationalized variables include knowledge extraction accuracy measured by the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), interpretability scores from user feedback, and computational efficiency metrics derived from training logs. Evaluation metrics will include the F1 score and interpretability assessment scores. To control for confounding variables, the study will use a standardized dataset and implement ablation studies to isolate the effects of the structured ontology and attention mechanisms. The scope will be limited to biomedical literature, with reproducibility ensured through open-source model access and established annotation protocols.

proposal: This proposal defends the claim that integrating attention mechanisms and structured ontology models within a Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework significantly enhances the accuracy and interpretability of knowledge extraction and document classification in biomedical literature compared to traditional text-mining techniques. The core gap identified is the lack of effective models that reconcile computational efficiency with interpretability in GNNs for knowledge extraction across diverse scientific domains. Current literature reveals a tension where existing models either lack contextual understanding or suffer from issues like LLM hallucination, necessitating a novel approach. The proposed research aims to develop a GNN framework that integrates structured ontology models to enhance contextual understanding and attention mechanisms to focus on relevant document features, leading to improved accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction tasks. This integration is theoretically grounded in the premise that structured ontologies provide a richer context for feature extraction, while attention mechanisms enhance the model's focus on pertinent information, thus improving performance. The falsifiable hypothesis posits that this integration will yield higher accuracy in knowledge extraction, as measured by the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), compared to traditional text-mining techniques, which will serve as the strongest baseline for comparison. A negative result would indicate that the proposed integration does not enhance knowledge extraction as hypothesized, suggesting a need to reassess the theoretical framework or the efficacy of the methodologies employed. To ensure methodological rigor, the proposal includes detailed descriptions of baseline comparisons, controls, and ablation studies to isolate the contributions of the structured ontology and attention mechanisms, thereby addressing the identified weaknesses in experimental design and literature engagement.
